title: First bands: Kid Howard and Don Raymond
summary: He worked with Kid Howard, struggled with unfamiliar tunes, then enjoyed playing with Don Raymond; Dixieland standards and waltzes.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Do you remember the first band you ever played with or group or first job you ever got when you decided you'd be good enough to go out and try to play?

The first band I really enjoyed playing with after I began to read pretty good. You know, Don Raymond. I worked with Kit Howard before that and I had kind of a hard time. I couldn't catch on to a lot of the things they were doing. No.

No. Do you know most of those pieces from hearing people around? That is, I don't know if you were too small to go to dances naturally when you were a kid, but like all these old Dixieland tunes as they call them, did you know most of those or the pieces they played just from hearing them? Like maybe sometime on the street the brass band plays them. Did you ever, or did you have to really work hard to learn all of those tunes? Like, well say even St. Louis Blues or Tiger Rag or different things they play quite often.
Well I remember playing St. Louis Blues, Tiger Rag, Bill Bok, Bell Poker, China Bar, some of the tunes I liked.
I know, Kit Howard knows so many pieces, he's unusual, he knows so many numbers.
And he played quite a few waltzes too.
You have to learn the waltzes too.
Well I got experience by doing that too. And just like I said, they called numbers that I never heard before and I had trouble with them.
And they tried to fake them.
